title: Choose the look for East DECA Prep
question: Every option uses your white/grey base, dark blue and gold, plus the cougar. They differ in the one signature idea that makes the app feel like Downingtown East. Pick one, or re-roll.

options.label: Gym Scoreboard
options.lineage: The scoreboard over the Downingtown East gym floor
options.thesis: Your study numbers are kept on the home scoreboard: today's count, streak, accuracy and the mock clock glow in gold on a navy board.
materials: gold lit numerals over unlit ghost segments
options.viewport: Navy top bar with cougar and nav; a slim navy scoreboard strip (TODAY 18/25 · STREAK 6 · ACCURACY 74%) over a white question card with four large answer buttons.
options.risk: If the board spreads past numbers it turns into a sports costume; it has to stay a strip, not a theme.

raised.raise: Gold is reserved for the live thing only: the current question, the running clock, the active tab. Never decoration.
A stat that changed since your last visit keeps a gold tick until you've seen it.
Scoreboard numerals appear at exactly three size steps across the whole app.
The PI code is set identically everywhere, as each question's catalog number.
All greys come from one fixed nine-step ramp; no one-off neutrals.

options.label: Answer Sheet
options.lineage: The bubble answer sheet the cluster exam is actually taken on
options.thesis: Practice the way you'll compete: choices are bubbles you fill, and the mock navigator is the 100-bubble answer sheet.
materials: oval answer bubbles filled in navy
gold check on the correct bubble
options.viewport: White page, navy header with cougar; the question set large with A–D as bubble rows; a mini 25-row answer column on the right shows the session so far.
options.risk: Ruling and timing marks can slide into nostalgia; the sheet idea must live only in bubbles and the grid.

options.label: Swipe Feed
options.lineage: Full-screen vertical feeds students scroll every day
options.thesis: One question owns the whole screen; answer, then flick to the next, with bookmark, flag and explain stacked on a right rail.
options.viewport: Phone-first: a navy full-height card with the question, four stacked answers low, rail glyphs on the right, next question one snap away.
options.case: Students know this motion by heart (wins on familiarity), but dashboards, filters and the mock navigator have no natural home in a feed.
options.risk: On Chromebooks it becomes a stretched phone; the dashboard has to break the feed rules.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Study as a course run control to control over a fixed terrain map.
options.viewport: Areas as terrain, today's session as a purple course.
options.case: Students don't know this world, and terrain colors fight the pinned blue and gold.
options.risk: Unreadable to anyone who hasn't orienteered.
options.kept: One color reserved strictly for the active item.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.thesis: Weak areas rerank like departures; a mock is your boarding pass.
options.viewport: A board of areas ranked by weakness.
options.case: Less personal than the school's own gym, and less clear than plain stats.
options.risk: Travel theme on a study tool.
options.kept: Changes stay highlighted until you've noticed them.

options.label: Bitmap Type Specimen
options.thesis: Pixel display type at poster scale over fine text.
options.viewport: A pixel headline over dense question text.
options.case: No tie to the chapter, and pixel type hurts reading long stems.
options.kept: One numeral form repeated at a few strict size steps.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything a numbered catalog entry on matte black.
options.viewport: A black field with one white data plot.
options.case: Black ground breaks the white/grey brief; codes replace words students need.
options.kept: A consistent catalog number on every item (the PI code).

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over a zone ramp, hatching for load.
options.case: Foreign to students and visually busy for a quiz.
options.kept: All neutrals from one fixed tonal ramp.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean study app like the big flashcard sites, done carefully in navy, grey and gold.
canonCard.viewport: Left navy sidebar with cougar and nav, white question card centered, progress bar on top.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other study site; nothing says Downingtown East but the logo.
